HO00004672.title: DocHouse: While We Watched
HO00004672.description: A gripping newsroom drama, following broadcast journalist Ravish Kumar as he fearlessly tackles misinformation and incompetent governance in India. Kumar and his team at NDTV fight tirelessly to report on the stories overlooked by pro-government mainstream media. However, this is no easy feat as, increasingly, many sensationalise criticism of the Modi government as treason. With fervent nationalism on the rise, dissidents are labelled as enemies of India, with their lives and livelihoods viciously attacked. With budget cuts, mass resignations and mounting death threats, can Kumar persevere in the face of adversity? While We Watched is a riveting tale of truth, courage and journalistic integrity. Kumar’s unyielding spirit is captured brilliantly, and we watch as he faces seemingly unending challenges. With factual reporting in international crisis, director Vinay Shukla trains his lens on a beleaguered lone voice, providing us with hope that there are still determined forces dedicated to speaking truth to power."

HO00007239.title: Curzon Film 50: The Double Life of Véronique

HO00007240.title: Curzon Film 50: The Gleaners and I
HO00007240.description: Varda films and interviews gleaners in France in all forms, from those picking fields after the harvest to those scouring the dumpsters of Paris.

HO00007337.title: DocHouse: A Free Daughter of Free Kyrgyzstan
HO00007337.description:
In Kyrgyzstan, domestic violence is on the rise, conservative groups are gaining political influence, and their young democracy is faltering. It is within this context that 21-year old singer and activist, Zere Asylbek, fearlessly speaks out against the injustices that women face in her country.
In this intimate, verité-style film, Zere reflects on her experience of becoming an overnight viral sensation, causing her to receive death threats and make international headlines. Despite being labeled as an "Agent of the West", she continues to rise as a voice of resistance, until the threats become too great.

HO00007292.title: DocHouse: Among Mountains and Streams
HO00007292.description:
In a mysterious forest, far from the borders of the China they’ve left behind, the painter Meng Huang and writer Ma Jian talk about exile, political opposition and artistic creation as a response to oppression and lies.
The dissident writer, who has been unable to return to China, where all of his books are banned, since 2011, and the renowned painter living in exile in Berlin, are haunted by memories of the country they have fled. As leaves fall around them, they journey through the forest contemplating persecution, resistance and the role of their work. For the two artists, whose world view has been upended by the Tiananmen Square massacre, creation offers an answer.

HO00007227.title: DocHouse: Ask E. Jean
HO00007227.description:
Across a five-decade career, E. Jean Carroll has emerged as a trailblazing journalist, talk show host and beloved advice columnist, conquering the male dominated publishing world of 1980s and 90s New York with a fearless voice all her own. 

In recent years, she has fought a high profile legal battle against Donald Trump for sexual assault and defamation, becoming the only woman to beat him in court. Twice. ASK E. JEAN is both a portrait of the thrilling, storied life of a singular icon, and a gutsy exploration of what it takes for a woman to stand up to power and prove she is telling the truth about a historic assault. With the multi-million dollar bill for damages still unpaid and the legal battle rumbling on through the courts and the headlines, ASK E. JEAN is critical viewing.

HO00007336.title: DocHouse: Celtic Utopia
HO00007336.description:
After 100 years of independence, a bold new wave of young Irish artists redefine folk music and reflect on the impact of their colonial history.

The Irish folk music renaissance sees artists coming from punk, hip-hop, and beyond, rediscovering an ancient tradition and taking it in unexpected directions. 

In CELTIC UTOPIA, artists including The Mary Wallopers, The Deadlians, Poor Creature, Negro Impacto and Lankum take us on a ballad tour around the island, telling stories and singing songs to try to understand their past and to heal their colonial wounds. Archive footage ties the present moment to Ireland’s troubled past, and creates a rich portrait of an island coming to terms with a century of independence.

HO00007184.title: DocHouse: David Byrne's American Utopia
HO00007184.description:
Do we get stupider as we grow up?’ In his wildly popular Broadway show American Utopia, David Byrne reflects on human connections, life and how on earth we work through it.
He joins the dots with his music and it all starts making sense. Spike Lee here transforms the production into immersive, dynamic cinema that radiates with astounding performances, inventive contemporary dance and political urgency. American Utopia flows like an iridescent dream vision. Work by James Baldwin, Janelle Monáe and Kurt Schwitters is highlighted among exhilarating renditions of Byrne’s solo work, as well as Talking Heads classics.

According to the multi-hyphenate, we love looking at humans more than anything else. Anti-fascist and anti-racist, Byrne illuminates our responsibility to care for one another as he and his co-performers burn down the house.

HO00007142.title: DocHouse: Disciples
HO00007142.description:
On the banks of the Ganges in Varanasi, two boys enter a revered Hindu school where lessons in ancient scripture blur into something more troubling.

Eleven-year-olds Satyarth and Hari join a traditional Sanskrit institution run by charismatic Guru Avimuktesh, shaving their heads, donning saffron robes and severing ties with the outside world. What initially appears as rigorous spiritual education gradually reveals a deeper intent, as devotion to ancient texts becomes entangled with caste hierarchy, religious prejudice and nationalist ideology.

Filmed with rare, intimate access over the course of a year, DISCIPLES captures how faith and identity are shaped in childhood, raising urgent questions about what is really being taught when no one is watching.

HO00005571.title: DocHouse: Farming The Revolution
HO00005571.description:
A stirring account of peaceful mass protest, Farming the Revolution follows the year-long Indian farmers' protest of 2020, an outcry in response to the country's newly enacted agricultural laws.

Driving tractors from Punjab to the border of Delhi, bringing food to share and setting up camp, over half a million protesters gathered - men and women from all generations, religions, classes and castes - determined to hold their ground until the laws were repealed.

Nishtha Jain's expansive portrait invites us to experience the everyday textures and indomitable spirit of this unprecedented movement, which culminated in an historic, triumphant outcome.

HO00007282.title: DocHouse: Gaza's Twins, Come Back to Me
HO00007282.description:
When Rania's newborn babies are evacuated from a hospital in northern Gaza to safety in the south, her family is suddenly torn apart - separated by a travel ban, military checkpoints and the turmoil of war.

What follows is an intimate dual portrait, following their parallel lives over sixteen months, and capturing Rania's extraordinary resilience.

From the bombed-out streets of northern Gaza to the overcrowded tents of the south, and from makeshift shelters to the shattered city, this deeply-felt film traces the journey of a family separated and a mother fighting to be reunited with her children.

HO00007290.title: DocHouse: Hanging by a Wire
HO00007290.description:
When a cable car wire snaps, eight passengers - including six schoolboys - are left dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the Himalayan foothills.
Director Mohammed Ali Naqvi tells the story of the nail-biting rescue mission that follows. With no margin for error and a single cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of civilian rescuers, police and military forces must improvise under intense public scrutiny, in a race against the clock before disaster strikes.
HANGING BY A WIRE combines staggering drone footage from the day with visceral reconstructions, and interviews with the extraordinary people who risked life and limb to reach the boys.

HO00007323.title: DocHouse: How Deep is Your Love
HO00007323.description:
With mesmerising underwater cinematography, HOW DEEP IS YOUR LOVE takes us way down below the surface with a team of scientists exploring the unknown: the deep sea, where 70% of our planet lies hidden.

Their life's work is finding, describing and naming strange and wonderful deep sea creatures, and now they find themselves racing against the looming threat of deep-sea mining, as they search for thriving ecosystems in the unexplored darkness.

Director Eleanor Mortimer weaves wonder with urgency, challenging us to balance the drive for resources with the intrinsic value of an ecosystem. As we journey through this breathtaking realm, we are left to ponder – how deep is our love?

HO00007230.title: DocHouse: How to Feed a Dictator
HO00007230.description:
This film tells the story of five brutal regimes, from Iraq to North Korea, through the eyes of the personal chefs who served them.

Through recipes, rituals and remembrance, a portrait emerges of power, manipulation and the quiet ways ordinary people become entangled in extraordinary violence. Loyalty, denial, fear, even thrill, each chef carries their experience differently, yet together they reveal how dictatorship gets under the skin of everyone it touches. HOW TO FEED A DICTATOR is darkly funny, deeply human and impossible to shake, proof that the most revealing place to understand a regime is not the war room but the kitchen.

HO00007320.title: DocHouse: My Armenian Phantoms
HO00007320.description:
MY ARMENIAN PHANTOMS is a docu essay in which personal (filmmaker’s father was the prominent actor Vigen Stepanyan) and public (a subjective history of Armenian film) are interwoven. In MY ARMENIAN PHANTOMS Tamara Stepanyan plunges into the Soviet Armenian cinema “with a sense of loss and disappearance” chasing its and her own shadows and ghosts. The resulting film reveals the enduring soul of Armenian storytelling — its beauty, its struggles, and its spirit.

Through the history(ies) of cinema, the filmmaker who left Armenia after the collapse of the Soviet Union explores what “being Armenian” actually means today.

HO00007281.title: DocHouse: Okurimono
HO00007281.description:
After 20 years abroad, Noriko returns to Nagasaki to clear out her late mother's home. Sorting through long-hidden letters, she begins to excavate a past never spoken of, unearthing a family history entwined with the atomic bomb that fell on 9th August 1945.

Eight decades later, the legacy of the bomb hangs heavy like a mist over Nagasaki, as Noriko visits survivors and digs into a past that will help her to heal in the present. 

Every word of testimony is uttered with dignity, and set against poignant images of the landscapes of Nagasaki. Through filmmaker Laurence Lévesque’s thoughtful storytelling and beautiful cinematography, OKURIMONO navigates the delicate realms of past collective trauma with grace, as it gradually becomes a meditation on remembrance and closure.

HO00007339.title: DocHouse: Sherman's March
HO00007339.description:
Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman’s 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South.
A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, SHERMAN’S MARCH is a landmark of first-person filmmaking that presaged everything from Michael Moore to reality TV. Now restored in beautiful 4k.

HO00007294.title: DocHouse: Shorts: Maybe Tomorrow + Allies in Exile
HO00007294.description:
This double bill of short films from exceptional Syrian filmmakers brings together stories of the bonds of friendship, displacement, loss and endurance during Assad's regime and in the precarious time since its sudden end.

MAYBE TOMORROW, directed by Wafa Mustafa and Waad Al-Kateab (FOR SAMA) follows Wafa's long search for her father, who was disappeared under Assad's regime. In ALLIES IN EXILE, filmmakers and friends Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al Halabi turn from documenting the frontlines of a revolution to filming the bureaucracy of exile whilst housed in a UK asylum hotel.

HO00007321.title: DocHouse: Skyclimber
HO00007321.description:
SKYCLIMBER follows 24-year-old urban free solo climber Adam Lockwood as he attempts to scale the Eiffel Tower without ropes or safety equipment, in a film that is equal parts high-altitude adventure and moving personal portrait.

Filmmaker Nick Hardie follows Adam’s journey from a turbulent childhood in Wigan through periods of homelessness and prison, to becoming one of the world’s most revered urban climbers and one of the global free solo community’s youngest stars.

Tackling the Eiffel Tower will take all of Adam's determination and months of planning and training, as he maps every step of the audacious ascent. Running along side adrenalin-filled journey and sequences of Adam's exhilarating climbs, is the story of a young man taking in neurodivergence, loss and the weight of men's mental health.

HO00007256.title: DocHouse: Soul to Soul
HO00007256.description:
In 1971, a group of the greatest African American soul, jazz and gospel artists travelled to Ghana for a historic, once-in-a-lifetime performance.

Artists including Ike & Tina Turner, Wilson Picket, The Staples Singers and Santana journeyed from New York to Accra, for an epic performance in front of 100,000 people, to celebrate 14 years since Ghana gained independence from Britain. 

For most of the artists, it would be their first trip to Africa - a journey exploring personal roots, ancestral homeland, history, loss, pain and joy. As well as electrifying performances, Denis Sanders's SOUL TO SOUL captures the artists as they visit local villages and meet Ghanaian performers, sharing their music and movement.

Little seen since its first release, but newly restored and re-released 55 years on, SOUL TO SOUL now takes its place as one of the great concert docs, and a galvanising record of cultural exchange.

HO00007254.title: DocHouse: Steal This Story, Please!
HO00007254.description: Fiercely independent journalist Amy Goodman has spent three decades holding the powerful to account, reporting from war zones and the Democracy Now! newsroom. In STEAL THIS STORY, PLEASE!  Oscar-nominated filmmakers Carl Deal and Tia Lessin craft a riveting portrait of journalism’s power – and peril – in an era of corporate control and political attacks on truth.

HO00007291.title: DocHouse: Super Nature
HO00007291.description:
A love letter to nature filmed exclusively on Super 8 (the original and beloved home movie format), SUPER NATURE invites us on a cinematic and richly rewarding global tour of connection with the natural world. 
To capture the whole world on camera, director Ed Sayers collaborated with 40 people filming the nature closest to their homes and their hearts on 80 different Super 8 cameras - across the land, in the air and under water. 

A celebration of all we have and a reflection on all we have to lose, this global co-creation project journeys across 25 different countries, creating a visceral, poetic and personal meditation on the world we live in.

HO00007322.title: DocHouse: The Cycle Of Love
HO00007322.description:
In 1977, PK, a young street artist from Delhi, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile journey to find the woman who had captured his heart.

Growing up poor and 'untouchable', young PK had to reckon with the caste system and with his own sense of self-worth, as he met fellow travellers and locals from all walks of life on his journey across the world. Oscar-nominated director Orlando von Einsiedel retraces PK's journey from India to Sweden in an extraordinarily uplifting film, that is not just about what can happen when you follow your heart, but is also a paean to the joy of chance encounters and the kindness of strangers.

HO00007293.title: DocHouse: The Gardener, The Buddhist and the Spy
HO00007293.description:
A corporate spy in the pocket of the asbestos industry, or a whistleblower uncovering corruption? When Rob Moore invites two journalists to tell his story, the lines between intentions and consequences begin to blur.
For five years, former TV producer Rob poses as a filmmaker to gain the trust of anti-asbestos activists, whilst being paid to spy on them by the asbestos industry. When he is exposed as a cynical fraud, he claims to be a double agent, working alone to feed  false information to the international asbestos mafia.

In a bid to launder his reputation and regain credibility, Rob lets two journalists begin work on a podcast about him, but as they delve deeper into the shady case, inconsistencies and ethical dilemmas cast doubt on Rob's version of events.  One twist leads to another in a gripping film about the delicate balance between good, evil, influence and control.

HO00007338.title: DocHouse: The Watergate Caper
HO00007338.description:
This archival documentary traces the rise and fall of Nixon from the presidential primaries of 1968 through the Watergate break-in of June 1972 to his resignation two years later, killing trust in the political process and the American presidency in the wake of the Vietnam War.
 The film draws on hundreds of hours of TV news taped off-air by the Nixon White House to tell the untold story of the Watergate burglars. How did tapping the wrong phone with a bug that didn't work lead to their arrests and Nixon's resignation? It also explores representations of the Nixon years in popular culture, using the music, commercials, and cinema of the era to evoke a fevered political landscape of culture wars, dirty tricks, paranoia and assassination. Sound familiar?

HO00007266.title: DocHouse: What We Were and What We Are
HO00007266.description:
First-time directors from the Sahrawi Refugee camps explore how their culture has changed after 50 years of enforced displacement. World Premiere screening of films and a Q&A. Organised by IRSAAN, UCL and UAL

WHAT WE WERE AND WHAT WE ARE is an event centered on a World Premiere screening of documentary films made by first-time directors from the Sahrawi Refugee camps. The young filmmakers have made works about their elders and how the Sahrawi culture has changed after 50 years of enforced displacement. The event will also comprise of talks and opportunities for Q&A sessions with the filmmakers and members of IRSAAN a Sahrawi led health charity based in the camps.

HO00007335.title: DocHouse: Yuja
HO00007335.description: Daredevil. Rebel. Powerhouse. At 39, Yuja Wang stands among the most electrifying musicians of our time and she is falling out of love with the music. In YUJA, acclaimed filmmaker Lorna Tucker crafts an immersive portrait of an artist in flux. With unprecedented access, the film weaves together performance, memory, and reconstruction to explore the forces that shape Yuja, and the woman she is still becoming.

HO00007340.title: The Final Film Festival: Plane Film + Q&A
HO00007340.description:
In an effort to continue using filmmaking as exposure therapy (after conquering her fear of the Tube in Tube Film), filmmaker Orla Smith tackles an even bigger fear: planes. On a trip to Porto, the camera is wielded as a shield against panic attacks. But this time, things don’t go exactly to plan.

I worried that without a film to work, on I wasn’t happy”, reads a text box at the start of Plane Film, a personal documentary / anxiety spiral by filmmaker Orla Smith. This encore screening follows the film’s competition win at The Final Film Festival (it won the recently christened Final d’Or), and it fits well with the festival’s name, as Plane Film is a film that restlessly wonders whether cinema is helping or hurting us.

Confronting air travel also forces Orla to confront something else: her compulsive need to document herself through her films as a form of self-administered therapy — or is it avoidance? A camera has helped her overcome some of her biggest fears, but it has also been a way to put distance between herself and the people around her. Plane Film is a film at war with itself, and with the concept of filmmaking in general. Should we throw the whole thing away? Should this be the final film festival after all? 

- Orla Smith
